mis_merges.label: ai narrative
mis_merges.why: The Anthropic-researcher safety warning (10m+ views) is a distinct sentiment/narrative-risk story, not evidence for the 'AI stocks bouncing off technical resistance' trade setup, and burying it here could cause an editor to miss it as its own theme.

mis_merges.label: midterm election seasonality
subjects: Equity seasonality trading strategy around midterms (buy healthcare, size up risk on Election Day)
Political race/prediction-market odds (Senate control) and its link to Iran conflict and Fed appointments
mis_merges.why: A tactical seasonality trade and a political-handicapping/geopolitics-meets-Fed-appointments piece are different theses a pulse would not fold into one brief; merging them risks the political-odds angle never surfacing as a theme.

mis_merges.label: ai infrastructure demand
subjects: Market Ear signal of AI enterprise spend deceleration (bearish demand datapoint)
Broadcom/Goldman AI infrastructure buildout guidance, demand outstripping supply (bullish supply-side narrative)
mis_merges.why: These are opposing reads (softening demand vs. supply-constrained bull case) that could anchor a bull-vs-bear AI capex debate; bundled under one label they read as one uniform demand narrative and the bearish counter-signal could be dropped.

mis_merges.label: european equity buy ideas
mis_merges.why: Three unrelated single-name/country calls (Germany macro thesis, a Greek banking-sector field trip, and an Inditex earnings model update) are stapled together; an editor scanning labels could easily miss the Inditex or Greek-banks story as its own brief.

notes: Fragmentation stays under the 10% threshold (~8.9%) but is concentrated in three big macro stories (Fed hikes, long-end yields, Middle East oil risk) each split 3-5 ways, seemingly by originating bank rather than subject. Four grab-bag labels mis-merge genuinely distinct subjects in ways that would change which themes an editor selects, so the metric fails on the mis-merge criterion.
